subtype: Approach: if-then rules for pressure situations [Thinking]
passage:
Sunday.
After what happened to Suhana at tuition, when a boy kept pushing and she froze and didn't know what to say, I made myself a rule and I'm writing it here so it's real. IF anyone keeps pushing after I say no, THEN I leave the conversation right away and tell an adult, Amma or Ms Bose. No debate, no explaining, no maybe later. I tested it in my head with Jomon, who is nice but keeps asking me to sit next to him at lunch and pouts when I say no. I've said no twice. If he asks a third time, I'll say, “I said no,” pick up my tray and go. Then I tell Ms Bose. It feels good to know the answer in advance, so I don't have to negotiate with my heart racing.
— Aadhya

qa.q: Who will Aadhya tell if someone keeps pushing?
qa.a: Aadhya will tell an adult, Amma or Ms Bose.

qa.q: How does Aadhya feel about having the rule?
qa.a: Aadhya feels relieved and more confident, since knowing the answer in advance means no negotiating with a racing heart.

qa.q: What could Aadhya do if someone follows or messages Aadhya after the conversation ends?
qa.a: Aadhya could save the messages, block the person and tell Amma or Ms Bose the same day.

qa.q: How might Jomon see Aadhya saying I said no?
qa.a: Jomon may feel surprised or embarrassed, but the boundary is clear and shows that Jomon needs to stop.

grounding: A teen decides that if anyone pushes after a no, the teen leaves the conversation and tells an adult, so there is a ready response and no need to negotiate.

passage:
Hrithik: you went quiet in the group after that joke
Disha: yeah. been thinking about something
Disha: at the party last month someone kept asking me to go outside with him. I said no like four times and just stood there feeling awkward
Hrithik: that sounds horrible
Disha: I talked it through with Mom that night. she helped me make a rule for myself
Disha: IF someone pushes after I say no ONCE, THEN I leave the conversation and tell an adult. no second explaining
Hrithik: why so strict
Disha: because under pressure my brain goes blank. if the answer is already decided I don't have to negotiate
Hrithik: makes sense. who's the adult
Disha: Mom at home, Ms. Rao at school, or whoever is hosting
Hrithik: can I use the same rule
Disha: obviously. it works for anyone

qa.q: Who are the adults Disha would tell?
qa.a: Mom at home, Ms. Rao at school, or whoever is hosting.

qa.q: Why does Disha want the answer decided in advance?
qa.a: Disha felt awkward and stuck at the party because the mind goes blank under pressure, so a ready rule feels safer than negotiating.

qa.q: What could make Disha's rule easier to use at a party?
qa.a: Agreeing with a friend like Hrithik to leave together, and knowing who the host is, would make the leaving part quick.

qa.q: How does Hrithik see the rule?
qa.a: Hrithik first finds it strict, then sees the sense in it and wants to use it too.

grounding: Shows a teen setting an if-then rule to leave and tell an adult whenever someone pushes after a no, so there is nothing to negotiate under pressure.

subtype: Approach: if-then rules for pressure situations [Thinking]
passage: Every evening, Vishal waited at the bus stand in Nawalgarh with his motorbike. "Ganga, sit, I'll drop you. Why walk in this heat?" She always said no. He always asked again. Walking home along the canal road, Ganga worked it out in her head. Arguing didn't help; every time she explained, he found a new reason. So: if he asks after I've said no once, then I stop talking, go into Bhagwati aunty's shop and phone Papa. No explaining, no waiting to see. The next evening he rolled the bike beside her. "One ride. What's the problem?" "No." "Come on, Ganga..." She turned, walked straight into the shop and asked for the phone. Papa came on his cycle within ten minutes, and that same evening he and Bhagwati aunty went to speak to the shopkeepers at the bus stand about Vishal.

qa.q: Where did Vishal wait every evening?
qa.a: Vishal waited at the bus stand in Nawalgarh.

qa.q: Why did Ganga decide to stop explaining?
qa.a: Ganga felt worn down and uneasy that each explanation only gave Vishal a new reason, so she wanted a fixed response that needed no arguing.

qa.q: What else could Ganga add to her plan?
qa.a: She could walk home with a friend and let her teacher know about Vishal too, so more adults are watching out.

qa.q: How is Papa affected by the phone call?
qa.a: Papa takes it seriously, coming within ten minutes and speaking to the shopkeepers that evening, so Ganga is not left to handle Vishal alone.

grounding: Illustrates a teen deciding in advance that if someone pushes after her no, she leaves and calls an adult, and then using that rule.
